title: Tech Note: Database Schemas and Security
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note documents the schema feature introduced in 4D v11 SQL Release 3, which enabled granular access control for external SQL/ODBC connections by assigning read, read-write, or full access to named schemas at the group level. The DEFAULT_SCHEMA and schema-based access model it describes remain conceptually relevant in 4D's modern SQL architecture, though the specific SQL syntax and preferences UI have evolved considerably. The componentized schema editor tool included with the note demonstrates 4D v11's capability-building approach through components and macros.
related_updates: 4D v17+ (Project Mode era) introduced ORDA and modern REST security paradigms, reducing reliance on SQL-level schema permissions
4D Web Security model evolved to handle both internal and external access via dedicated role-based systems rather than group-based schema grants
The visual schema editor component architecture is now deprecated in favor of built-in Design Center and Project Model tooling
